input.body:
## The risk

The hook `useKeyboardShortcuts` read the `when` clause of each shortcut. It made a code string from the clause. Then it ran the string with `new Function()`.

Two defects were present:

1. `new Function()` runs code from a string. This is a code-injection risk. It also needs the `unsafe-eval` policy in the browser. A healthcare application must not allow this policy.
2. The old code put each condition value into the string as text. A condition value of the type string could add more code to the expression.

Today only `src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json` supplies the clauses. Every clause in that file is `always`. No plugin and no `care-apps` code supplies a clause. Thus the risk is low today. But the pattern is not safe, and a new clause can make the risk real.

## The fix

A new module `src/hooks/utils/evaluateShortcutCondition.ts` has a pure function. The function reads the tokens of the clause and calculates the result.

The evaluator accepts only these tokens:

- the literal `always`
- the literals `true` and `false`
- an identifier that names a key in `ShortcutConditions`
- the operators `!`, `&&` and `||`
- parentheses

The evaluator reads each value directly from the conditions object. It never makes a string of code. If the clause has an unknown token, the evaluator writes a warning and returns `false`. This is the same result as the old catch block.

The exported behaviour of `useKeyboardShortcuts` does not change. A clause of `always` still returns `true`.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` shows no new error.
- A temporary script gave 18 clauses to the evaluator. All results were correct. The script is deleted.
- `npx playwright test tests/facility/patient/encounter/encounterShortcuts.spec.ts` passed. All 17 tests passed. The 9 shortcut tests show that the shortcuts still work.

## The problem

The hook `useKeyboardShortcuts` read the `when` clause of each shortcut. It made a code string from the clause. Then it ran the string with `new Function()`.

Two defects were present:

1. `new Function()` runs code from a string. This is a code-injection risk. It also needs the `unsafe-eval` policy in the browser. A healthcare application must not allow this policy.
2. The old code put each condition value into the string as text. A condition value of the type string could add more code to the expression.

## The evidence

The `when` clause had the value `always` in all 108 entries of `src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json`. No other value was present.

```
$ python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json'));print(sorted({s['when'] for v in d.values() for s in v}))"
['always']
```

Only that static file supplies the shortcuts. No plugin and no `care-apps` code supplies a clause. The `conditions` parameter of the hook had one purpose: to feed the `when` clause. No caller read the filtered `shortcuts` result.

So the feature was dead code.

## The fix

This pull request deletes the feature. It is better to delete dead code than to keep an evaluator for it.

The change removes:

- the `when` field from all 108 entries in `src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json`
- the `when` field from the `KeyboardShortcut` interface
- the `ShortcutConditions` interface
- the `conditions` parameter of `useKeyboardShortcuts`
- the `new Function()` call

The hook keeps the same behaviour. All shortcuts were active before, because each clause was `always`. All shortcuts stay active now.

If a shortcut needs a condition later, the team can add a typed boolean field. A string clause is not necessary.

Update on PR #16725 — the approach changed after a review finding.

The `when` feature turned out to be entirely dead, so rather than keeping a safe evaluator for it, the whole feature is now deleted. One reviewer had flagged exactly this ("replaces a one-line `new Function()` with a 213-line hand-rolled parser").

Removed: the `when` field from all 108 JSON entries, the `when` field on `KeyboardShortcut`, the `ShortcutConditions` interface, the `conditions` parameter of `useKeyboardShortcuts`, the `new Function()` call, and the evaluator module added in the first commit.

Net diff vs `develop`: 4 files, 112 insertions, 161 deletions.

React Doctor `no-eval`: 1 → 0 (unchanged from before). Errors 21 → 20, warnings 1313 → 1312, score 43 → 45. The React Doctor CI check reports 0 errors and 0 warnings on the diff, score 92/100.

CI on the PR: lint, eslint, build, unit-tests, CodeQL, and all 3 Playwright shards pass. The only red checks belong to the "CARE PR Reviewer" agentic workflow, which gets cancelled by concurrency on each push — it is not related to this change.

Local checks: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run knip` clean, and `npx playwright test tests/facility/patient/encounter/encounterShortcuts.spec.ts` passed 17/17 against the local backend.

I replied to and resolved all 11 review threads, because each one referenced the deleted evaluator file. The PR title and body are updated to describe the removal.
